analysis.one_liner: Hindustan Unilever sells India's biggest portfolio of personal care, home care, beauty and food brands (Dove, Surf Excel, Lifebuoy, Lipton), after spinning off its ice-cream business (Kwality Wall's) into a separate listed company in December 2025.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results (declared 28 Oct 2026): revenue of roughly ₹18,100 crore, up ~15% year-on-year and the fastest underlying sales growth in 14 quarters, with underlying volume growth of 7% - also a 14-quarter high. Reported net profit was about ₹2,790-2,796 crore, up only ~4% year-on-year (sources vary slightly), while EBITDA rose 8% to ₹4,089 crore. The board declared an interim dividend of ₹19/share with record date 12 November 2026 and payment on 25 November 2026 - under two weeks away.
analysis.plain_terms: This is India's largest FMCG company by sales, and this quarter it finally showed the volume recovery investors have waited years for - people are buying more units, not just paying higher prices. But the stock itself has been a poor investment: it's down more than a third from its 2024 peak and has badly trailed the market for three and five years. Part of that apparent fall is misleading because in December 2025 HUL gave shareholders a separate share in its spun-off ice-cream company (Kwality Wall's) - value the raw share price chart doesn't show. The honest tension is: operations are improving, but the price has not caught up, and profit growth (4%) is lagging revenue growth (15%) because costs are rising too.
analysis.quarters: Underlying sales growth of 15% and volume growth of 7% in Q2 FY27 are both the best in 14 quarters, per management, helped by rural wage support (MSP hikes, MGNREGA) and sequential improvement over the last three-four quarters. However, this is the first full quarter after the Kwality Wall's ice-cream demerger completed in December 2025, so year-on-year revenue and volume comparisons mix a 'continuing operations' quarter against a base period that still included the ice-cream business - treat the 15% growth figure as not strictly like-for-like. Reported PAT grew only ~4% versus 15% revenue growth, implying margin compression from input-cost inflation; management says PAT before exceptional items was up a healthier ~9%.
analysis.performance_read: Long-term returns are poor and worsening: the stock is down 23% over 1 year, 20.5% over 3 years and 16% over 5 years, versus Nifty gains of 29% and 20.8% over the same 5- and 3-year windows respectively - a wide, sustained underperformance, not a recent blip. One adjustment matters: in the Dec-2025 demerger, HUL holders received one Kwality Wall's (India) share for every HUL share held, and analysts valued that standalone ice-cream business at only roughly ₹1,200-1,500 crore in aggregate - trivial next to HUL's own market capitalisation. So raw price returns slightly understate true shareholder return, but the omitted value is too small to meaningfully change the underperformance picture.
analysis.valuation_read: P/E estimates cluster around 28-30x in the most recent commentary (one outlier source cites ~39x, set aside as inconsistent with the rest). That is well below HUL's own 10-year median multiple (one source pegs the median near 60x), making it look cheap relative to its own history. Why it looks cheap: years of slow volume growth, FMCG-wide demand weakness, and demerger-related uncertainty have compressed the multiple. Whether it is actually cheap depends on whether this quarter's 7% volume growth is the start of a sustained re-rating or a one-off bump from rural wage support and a soft prior-year base - that is not yet established.
analysis.growth_read: Growth this quarter was a mix of both volume and price/mix: 7% volume growth (the structural, more durable signal) plus additional revenue from price increases taken against commodity inflation. Management frames it as consumption-led and credits brand investment, portfolio premiumisation and general-trade expansion (30,000 new outlets) rather than price alone - a genuinely more encouraging mix than past quarters where growth was largely pricing-led. It still needs more quarters to confirm as a trend.
analysis.health_read: HUL has historically run with very low debt and strong operating cash generation - a defining feature of its FMCG model. Current-quarter cash-conversion and balance-sheet debt figures were not independently verified in this check - check on Screener. The more relevant risk for this business is on the demand/competitive side (volume growth, market share versus regional and D2C FMCG players), not balance-sheet or financial risk.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter holding (Unilever Group) stands at 61.90%, unchanged recently, with zero shares pledged - no leverage risk at the promoter level. Institutional holders have shifted modestly: FII/FPI holding slipped from 9.50% to 9.26% and mutual fund holding rose from 7.15% to 7.42% in the latest quarter. There is no marquee individual investor on the register - as a large MNC-promoted blue-chip, HUL's ownership is dominated by the promoter and institutions rather than any well-known individual investor, and that absence is itself unremarkable for a stock of this type.
strengths: Underlying volume growth of 7% in Q2 FY27 is the highest in 14 quarters, suggesting a genuine demand pickup rather than price-led growth alone
EBITDA grew 8% year-on-year to ₹4,089 crore even while absorbing input-cost inflation
Zero pledge on the promoter's 61.90% stake removes any financial-engineering risk at the top of the register
Return ratios remain strong by FMCG standards, with ROCE commonly cited in the high-20s percent range
watchpoints: Stock is down ~36% from its September 2024 peak and has underperformed the Nifty by roughly 30-45 percentage points over 1, 3 and 5 years
Reported PAT growth of only ~4% year-on-year lagged 15% revenue growth, showing real margin pressure from costs
Q2 FY27 is the first full quarter after the December 2025 ice-cream demerger, so year-on-year growth figures are not fully comparable and should be read with that caveat
FII holding has been trimmed in recent quarters (9.50% to 9.26%), a modest but notable shift in institutional sentiment
analysis.one_thing: Whether the 7% volume growth seen in Q2 FY27 holds for another 2-3 quarters - that would confirm a genuine, durable demand recovery rather than a one-off bump from rural wage support and a soft year-ago base.
analysis.data_notes: Revenue and PAT figures for Q2 FY27 were cross-checked across Business Standard, 5paisa and GuruFocus and were broadly consistent (minor variation between ₹18,071-18,226 crore revenue and ₹2,790-2,796 crore PAT, likely rounding/reporting-basis differences). P/E and ROE estimates varied more widely across sources (P/E 28.5x-39.2x; ROE 21.7%-30.6%) - the lower, more frequently cited cluster was used and the high outliers set aside. Latest balance-sheet debt and detailed cash-conversion figures were not independently verified - check on Screener. Kwality Wall's (India) standalone valuation (₹1,200-1,500 crore) is an analyst estimate, not a verified market price, since it only recently listed.
